items.text: Components · When does a component get another look? → Also for emphasis and size
For an error message, use color.status.danger and a sentence. Don't use the brand color. Status colors are shared, never branded.
For a delete or remove, use button secondary, then confirm with Button danger. Don't use button primary. Confirm before destroying data.

When no component in the inventory fits, use a component from the inventory with brand tokens. Don't use a component made for one brand. Brands change primitives, never components; one brand-only part breaks the shared library.
Button's secondary variant. The alternative that steps back, and the first step of a delete.
Button's danger variant. The confirm of a delete, the same red in every brand: danger never follows the brand.
Badge's danger tone. Card declined: the payment failed, so the plan will stop.
Alert's destructive variant. A billing problem such as a declined card: plain and specific, the same in every brand.

brand-q3.answer: Each brand brings its own face, on one shared scale
brand-q3.why: Each brand brings its own face, Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans or Poppins, on one shared type scale, so brands differ and the system stays one.

items.label: Readability
items.text: All three are screen sans faces with open shapes; the shared scale keeps body size and line height the same in every brand.

items.label: Legibility
items.text: Each brand checks its face's confusable characters in its own data; the scale gives every brand the same sizes to check at.

items.label: Scalability
items.text: All three have a wide range of weights, so every role in the shared scale has a weight in every brand.

items.label: Numerals
items.text: Inter has tabular figures; the brands that show tables lean on it.

items.label: Scripts and languages
items.text: Latin, with accents, in all three; Poppins also covers Devanagari. Other scripts need a face per brand.

items.label: Recognition
items.text: The face is how each brand is known on a shared system.

items.label: Familiarity
items.text: Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans and Poppins are widely seen on the web, so none feels strange.

items.label: Personality
items.text: A neutral base each brand can color: the face carries the brand, the scale stays neutral.

items.label: Performance
items.text: One family per brand: a page loads only its own brand's face.

items.label: Licensing
items.text: SIL Open Font License, all three: free to embed in apps and on the web.

items.label: Fallback and pairing
items.text: Each falls back to system-ui, as its tokens say; the shared scale keeps the layout steady while a face loads.
